The single outermost dispatch is `_walk(cfn.template, {}, cfn)` (line 108 of `_language_extensions.py`); `_walk` then recursively walks the template per the rules at lines 111-198. Restricting the call-stack depth count to ONLY frames whose qualified name is `cfnlint.template.transforms._language_extensions._Transform._walk`, what is the MAXIMUM simultaneous depth of in-flight `_walk` frames reached during this test run? Dispatch rules (by FIRST dict key): (1) `Fn::ForEach::<...>`: iterate the literal-list collection in order and recurse on the iteration body with `params` extended by the loop var (one new `_walk` frame per iteration). After all iterations, DELETE the `Fn::ForEach` key. (2) `Fn::Sub` with a STRING value: run `_replace_string_params(v, params)`; if fully resolved, REPLACE the dict with the string. NO recursive `_walk`. (3) `Fn::Sub` with a LIST value: run `_replace_string_params(v[0], params)`; if fully resolved, return that string IMMEDIATELY (no recursion on v[1]); otherwise keep the dict and recursively walk v[1]. (4) `Fn::FindInMap`: instantiate `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap` and call `.value(...)`; on success (a scalar/list) return it IMMEDIATELY (no recursion on v); on ANY exception, recursively walk EACH element of v. (5) `Ref` with STRING value: if `v in params`, return `params[v]` IMMEDIATELY (no further recursion BUT the `_walk` frame for the dict containing `Ref` is still entered, so it counts toward depth). (6) Any other key: recursively walk the value; if the sub-walk returns `None`, delete the key. Each recursion adds one `_walk` frame. (7) On a list, walk each element in place (one `_walk` frame per element). (8) Strings, ints, floats and bools enter ONE `_walk` frame each (deepcopy-and-return tail). Note: the per-key ``${var}``-rename pass at lines 115-120 does NOT itself invoke `_walk` -- only `_replace_string_params` is called. Return the answer as the field `maximum_call_stack_depth`.

- `transform()` calls one initial `_walk(cfn.template, {}, cfn)`.
- In `_walk`, dict values recurse through the `else` branch at line 186.
- `Fn::ForEach` recurses on the iteration body once per collection element at lines 128–131.
- Lists recurse on each element at lines 195–197.
- `Ref` with a string in `params` returns immediately at line 178, but only after entering that `_walk` frame.
- Scalars still enter one `_walk` frame and then return at line 198.

Using the test template, the deepest nesting comes from following one branch all the way down before any returns:
1. root template dict
2. `"Resources"` value dict
3. outer `Fn::ForEach` body dict `{"Wrap${X}": ...}` for one `X`
4. `"Wrap${X}"` value dict
5. `"Properties"` value dict
6. `"Tags"` value dict
7. inner `Fn::ForEach` body dict `{"Tag${X}${Y}": ...}` for one `Y`
8. `"Tag${X}${Y}"` value list
9. first list element dict `{"Key": "k", "Value": {"Ref": "Y"}}`
10. `"Value"` value dict `{"Ref": "Y"}`

At that point, the `Ref` branch returns `params["Y"]` immediately, so depth does not increase further. The sibling `"Key": "k"` path is shallower because it goes to a scalar frame instead of another dict under `"Value"`. The second list element has the same shape and same maximum. No `Fn::Sub` or `Fn::FindInMap` branches are present in this test template, so nothing changes that maximum.
